VER-01.text: The shares trade at 3.1 times forward revenue, a discount to the 4.5 times average of high-growth infrastructure peers.

VER-02.text: Seven of ten covering analysts rate the stock Buy, with a median price target 38% above the current share price.

VER-03.text: One analyst downgraded the stock to Hold in October, citing concentration in a single customer.

VER-04.text: Proprietary fast-charging technology cuts charging time by 40% and is protected by 23 granted patents.

VER-05.text: Two utility-backed competitors announced rival charging networks in Verdant's core markets, and management said pricing pressure is beginning to emerge.

VER-06.text: Revenue grew 94% year over year to $1.12 billion as charging sessions on the network tripled.

VER-07.text: The order book reached a record $3.4 billion after the company signed a five-year deployment agreement with a major European logistics group.

VER-08.text: Gross margin improved to 31% from 22% as hardware costs fell and software subscriptions grew to 28% of revenue.

VER-09.text: Management raised full-year revenue guidance for the second time this year.

VER-10.text: Net debt to EBITDA of 3.2x at quarter end, up from 2.4x a year earlier, as the company borrowed to fund network expansion.

VER-11.text: Cash and committed facilities of $310 million equal about 19 months of runway at the current burn rate.

VER-12.text: The largest customer, the European logistics group, accounted for 56% of revenue, up from 41% a year earlier.

VER-13.text: The founder and chief executive owns 24% of the shares and has not sold any since the listing.

VER-14.text: The board added two independent directors with infrastructure finance experience this year.

claims.text: Revenue surged 94% year over year to $1.12 billion alongside a record order book of $3.4 billion, supported by a five-year deployment agreement with a major European logistics group.

Shares trade at an attractive 3.1 times forward revenue discount compared to the 4.5 times average of high-growth infrastructure peers, with seven of ten analysts rating the stock Buy and a median price target 38% higher than the current price.

Gross margin expanded strongly to 31% from 22% due to falling hardware costs and software subscriptions growing to account for 28% of revenue, leading management to raise full-year revenue guidance twice.
The company possesses proprietary fast-charging technology protected by 23 granted patents that cuts charging time by 40%.
The founder and CEO retains a 24% ownership stake with zero shares sold since listing, while governance is strengthened by the addition of two independent infrastructure finance directors.
The company faces severe customer concentration risk as its largest customer, a European logistics group, accounts for 56% of revenue, up from 41% a year earlier.
Net debt to EBITDA rose to 3.2x at quarter end from 2.4x a year earlier due to borrowings for network expansion.
Pricing pressure is beginning to emerge in core markets following the announcement of rival charging networks by two utility-backed competitors.
An analyst downgraded the stock to Hold in October specifically because of this concentration in a single customer.

rebuttals.response: While customer concentration has increased, this relationship is anchored by a record $3.4 billion order book backed by a five-year deployment agreement [VER-07], which underpins phenomenal 94% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.12 billion [VER-06].

While revenue and the order book appear impressive, this growth carries extreme customer concentration risk, as the single European logistics group now accounts for 56% of total revenue, up from 41% a year earlier.

judgement.rationale: Verdant Mobility demonstrates outstanding growth with revenues surging 94% and a record order book of $3.4 billion [VER-06, VER-07], supported by expanding gross margins and multiple guidance raises [VER-08, VER-09]. The valuation is attractive relative to peers [VER-01] alongside strong analyst backing [VER-02] and high insider ownership [VER-13]. Although customer concentration [VER-12] and rising debt [VER-10] present risks, the strong long-term deployment agreement [VER-07] and financial performance outweigh these concerns.
